title: Add `Color.to_named`

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Proposal: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12178.

Adds a method to `Color` called `to_named` which returns the (mathematically-) closest standardized color name to the color.
```gdscript
var white = Color(1, 1, 1, 0.5)
print(white.to_named()) # Prints "WHITE"
```
```csharp
var white = new Color(1, 1, 1, 0.5f);
GD.Print(white.ToNamed()); // Prints "WHITE"
```

The implementation loops through each standardized color and tracks the closest color by subtracting the components and calculating the squared distance.

### Performance

#### C++

According to an external benchmark by @Ivorforce, the worst-case of the C++ function takes about 0.09 microseconds (0.00000009 seconds) (omitting the `String` allocation) meaning it could be called over 185,000 times per frame at 60FPS.

#### C#

According to an external benchmark by myself, the worst-case of the C# function takes about 0.351 microseconds (0.000000351 seconds) meaning it could be called over 47,000 times per frame at 60FPS:

| Method                | Mean       | Error     | StdDev    |
|---------------------- |-----------:|----------:|----------:|
| DictionaryWorst       | 467.159 ns | 1.6780 ns | 1.4012 ns |
| FrozenDictionaryWorst | 351.904 ns | 1.8579 ns | 1.7379 ns |
| DictionaryBest        |   5.752 ns | 0.0251 ns | 0.0235 ns |
| FrozenDictionaryBest  |   5.366 ns | 0.0220 ns | 0.0205 ns |

The `Frozen` benchmarks refer to #105104.

## Potential Issues

### Returned case

**IMPORTANT**: Currently, since the C# dictionary keys are in `UPPERFLATCASE`, there is no way to convert to a different case. So that should be fixed, but it's a separate issue.

The C++ case keys are currently in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` meaning that would be returned here. However, the user is unlikely to want that case. It can be converted to another case for example `Title Case` (the case used by X11) using a string function like `Capitalize`, although that would result in more allocations.

### English-only (no translations)

The returned color name would be in English only, without options to translate to another language.

Since the other functions relating to color names are English-only anyway, this would likely be fine (as stated by @Zireael07 in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12178#issuecomment-2797141221).

However, since this function would almost certainly be used for displaying colors to the user rather than accepting colors on the programming side, it could be a bigger issue with this function.

### Performance

@Calinou suggested a faster version of this method would be:

> to create a 3D LUT using a palette that matches the web colors only, and sampling this 3D LUT on the CPU according to the color and return the color (which will always match a web color exactly).

However, since this function is so performant already, and its main use cases would only call it rarely, this optimisation was considered unnecessary by myself and @Ivorforce.

- _Bugsquad edit: closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12178_
